children: Shares of Trent Ltd, the Tata Group's retail arm, rallied over 6 percent in early trade on Friday, October 30, after the company reported strong earnings for the second quarter of the financial year 2026-27, with brokerages offering mixed outlook on the stock. While some flagged improving operating performance and margin resilience, others raised concerns over input cost inflation, valuations and the sustainability of profitability in the upcoming quarters.

Shares of Trent opened at Rs 3,015 and surged 6.30 percent to touch a high of Rs 3,059, compared with the previous close of Rs 2,866. At around 10.05 am, the stock was trading 6.17 percent higher at Rs 3042.70.
Trent Q2 results

Trent reported a 25 percent year-on-year increase in consolidated net profit to Rs 468 crore for the September quarter, as revenue growth and operating leverage supported earnings amid an inflationary environment.

The company’s consolidated revenue from operations rose 22 percent to Rs 5,873 crore in the quarter ended September 30, while operating earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation (EBITDA) increased 37 per cent to Rs 785 crore.
For the first half of FY27, consolidated revenue grew 20 per cent to Rs 11,628 crore and net profit rose 24 per cent to Rs 986 crore. Operating EBITDA increased 35 per cent to Rs 1,633 crore.

On a standalone basis, revenue from operations climbed 23 per cent to Rs 5,788 crore in the September quarter, while operating EBITDA rose 37 per cent to Rs 791 crore. Net profit increased 9 per cent to Rs 490 crore.

The slower growth in standalone profit compared with operating earnings partly reflects a higher base in the year-earlier period, which included non-operating gains from asset sales. Trent reported a pre-tax profit on asset sales of Rs 96 crore in Q2 FY26 and Rs 109 crore in H1 FY26, with no material corresponding gains in the current-year periods.
Trent's operating EBIT margin improved to 11.6 per cent in the September quarter from 10.5 per cent a year earlier, according to the company.
Trent also reported growth in its emerging categories, including beauty and personal care, innerwear and footwear, which contributed more than 21 percent of standalone revenue.
Trent's Star food and grocery business reported revenue growth of more than 20 percent during the quarter, despite a competitive operating environment.
Brokerages of Trent share price
Jefferies on Trent share: Hold, Target price Rs 3300
Global brokerage firm Jefferies maintained a ‘Hold’ rating on Trent with a target price of Rs 3,300, implying an upside of 15 percent compared to the previous day closing at Rs 2,866.
The brokerage said while revenue growth was already known from pre-quarter release, margin expansion drove 37 percent YoY increase in pre-Ind AS EBITDA -, although the performance missing estimates.

Jefferies noted that like-for-like (LFL) growth in the fashion business picked up mid-single-digit range despite a shift in festive seasonality. It said the results should boost investor sentiment and support the stock in the near term. However, the brokerage cautioned that higher input prices cloud near-term outlook for margins and potentially affect demand in the coming quarters.
HSBC on Trent share: Buy, Target price Rs 3480

HSBC retained its ‘Buy’ recommendation on Trent with a target price of Rs 3,480, implying an upside of 21 percent against the previous day close. The brokerage cited better-than-expected operating performance as the reason behind the positive outlook.
The brokerage said Q2 EBITDA beat its estimates by around 2 percent, driven by resilient gross margins despite expectations of pressure from raw material costs.
HSBC also highlighted a recovery in LFL growth to the mid-single-digit range from low-single-digit growth in Q1 FY27, despite festive shift.
The brokerage raised its FY28 EBITDA estimate by 2 percent, while marginally lowering its earnings-per-share estimate due to changes in other income.
Ambit Capital on Trent share: Buy, Target price 3,509
Ambit Capital maintained its ‘Buy’ rating with a target price of Rs 3,509, implying an upside of 22 percent from the previous day close.

The brokerage said like-for-like sales growth in Trent's fashion business improved to mid-single digits from low-single-digit growth in recent quarters, indicating improving demand at existing stores.
Ambit Capital said Trent's gross margin expanded about 120 basis points year-on-year to 44.5%, beating market expectations by 150 bps, aided by better sourcing and inventory management.
CITI on Trent share: Sell, Target price Rs 2,815

Brokerage Citi maintained a ‘Sell’ rating on Trent with a target price of Rs 2,815, despite acknowledging growth in revenue and operating performance were above estimates. The brokerage said revenue and EBITDA grew 23 percent and 30 percent YoY, respectively, coming in 4 percent and 1 percent above its estimates.
However, a 71 percent YoY decline in other income weighed on profitability, with net profit growth of 9 percent coming in 3 percent below Citi’s estimates.

Citi identified key positive surprise was gross margin, which expanded 121 bps YoY despite raw-material inflation. Pre-Ind AS rent and operating expenses per square foot declined 8 percent and 11 percent, respectively, while employee costs per square foot increased 5 percent YoY.
However, revenue per square foot declined 8.4 percent YoY, even as LFL growth improved to the mid-single-digit range.
The brokerage said the sustainability of margins amid raw material and operating-cost inflation in the second half of FY27 would be key for the stock’s performance.
While Citi said it continued to like Trent’s business model and execution track record but await better valuation or successful scale-up of new pilot formats to add new growth engines.

title: Trent shares jump 6% amid margin expansion in Q2; brokerages say 'Buy'
